# 美银证券：腾讯控股重申“买入”评级 目标价下调至700港元

美银证券：腾讯控股重申“买入”评级 目标价下调至700港元

 2026年11月24日 12:41 新浪港股

 美银证券发布研报称，将腾讯控股（00700）目标价由780港元下调10.3%至700港元，重申“买入”评级。该行在腾讯2026年第三季度财报发布后更新预测，认为宏观压力加剧，加上AI算力限制趋严，令其对近期每股盈利转趋审慎，但AI投资及宏观担忧已达高峰，而AI变现能力将逐步显现。

 腾讯仍是该行的行业首选，理由包括：AI转型与组织变革有助于精简团队，提升人力成本效益；美国对算力的新限制预计对腾讯财务造成的冲击小于同业，因其相关外部云收入占比较低，而中国在尖端模型发展上的进度较缓，亦给腾讯更多时间缩小模型能力差距；短剧及“微信小店”等新兴变现模式，在目前的市场预测中仍被低估。

 该行维持对腾讯2026年、2027年及2028年资本开支预测，分别为2，100亿元、2，600亿元及2，700亿元人民币，认为未来大幅增加的空间有限。随着在手算力增加及WorkBuddy产品推广，该行预计腾讯云收入在2027年将进一步加速增长，同比增幅有望超过40%。

BEIJING, Nov 18 (Reuters) - China’s Tencent Holdings said on Wednesday that new US restrictions on remote access to advanced AI chips would not substantially hurt its cloud revenue, though they would likely slow development of its next AI model.

Washington this week unveiled rules restricting remote access to advanced US AI chips through overseas data centres. Shares in Chinese cloud service providers, including Tencent, fell on Tuesday after the announcement.

"We actually don’t see an impact, because our cloud business today is primarily running inference," Chief Strategy Officer James Mitchell told analysts on a post-earnings call.

"We think that our cloud revenue will not be substantially adversely affected by the changes," he said.

Investing.com-- Tencent Holdings (HK:0700) shares fell on Thursday after the Chinese technology giant reported weaker-than-expected third-quarter earnings, raising concerns over the costs of its artificial intelligence expansion.

The Hong Kong-listed stock dropped 6.1% to HK$350 by 02:58 GMT, reaching its lowest since May 2024.

Results on Wednesday showed that revenue rose 8% year-on-year to 207.3 billion yuan ($31.1 billion) in the three months ended September, below the 210.8 billion yuan expected by analysts, according to LSEG data.

Non-IFRS operating profit fell 6% to 68.1 billion yuan, while adjusted net profit declined 6% to 66.5 billion yuan.

Tencent’s capital expenditure surged to 81.4 billion yuan from 52.8 billion yuan in the previous quarter as it ramped up investment in AI infrastructure. Payments for capital expenditure jumped 225% year-on-year to 65.1 billion yuan.

Gaming revenue grew just 3%, while fintech and business services revenue increased 9%, supported by demand for AI-related cloud services.

The results come as U.S. restrictions on access to advanced AI chips threaten to complicate China’s technology ambitions.
